anomalies.observed: On the second sheet, the SMD MCU U2 (ATtiny13V-10S) is drawn with pad1 labelled PB3 (net NET0008, the pot wiper), pad2 labelled PB4 (net NET0003, the 5V1 zener rail), and pad3 labelled RESET/PB5 (net NET0012, the ISP RST line). The THT U4 (ATtiny45-20P) on the same sheet correctly puts RESET/PB5 on pad1, PB3 on pad2 and PB4 on pad3.
anomalies.expected: The ATtiny13V datasheet pinout is pad1 = PB5/RESET, pad2 = PB3, pad3 = PB4 (identical to the ATtiny45 shown on U4). Therefore NET0012 (RST) must land on pad1, NET0008 (pot) on pad2 and NET0003 on pad3. U2's symbol pin-number-to-name mapping is rotated by one on pins 1-3, so the nets are wired to the wrong physical pads of the 8-pin footprint.

evidence.quote: U2 ATtiny13V-10S: pin1 PB3 -> NET0008, pin2 PB4 -> NET0003, pin3 RESET/PB5 -> NET0012 (sheet /, page 2 right tile)
U4 ATtiny45-20P: pin1 RESET/PB5 -> NET0012, pin2 XTAL1/PB3 -> NET0008, pin3 XTAL2/PB4 -> NET0003 (sheet /, page 2 middle tile)

anomalies.impact: If the SMD U2 footprint is populated, the chip's RESET pin is driven by the potentiometer instead of the ISP/reset net, the ISP RST line sits on PB4, and the analog pot input is misrouted. The microcontroller would be held in reset or otherwise misprogrammed, and the fan-control firmware could not run or be flashed via J8.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains one anomaly: the SMD MCU U2 (ATtiny13V-10S) has its pins 1-3 mis-mapped relative to the part's datasheet (and relative to the correctly-drawn U4), cross-wiring the RESET, PB3 and PB4 nets; everything else traced on the drawing is internally consistent.
